findings.current: The late Emperor had seriously considered ordering a campaign, but Baek Yeon had pleaded with him so earnestly—more than he had ever seen him do before—that the Emperor finally gave up the idea.
findings.defect: The nested pronouns make it unclear who had seen whom plead before.
findings.rationale: Preserves Baek Yeon’s unusually forceful opposition without the confusing point of comparison.
findings.replacement: The late Emperor had seriously considered ordering a campaign, but Baek Yeon had pleaded with him more earnestly than ever before, until the Emperor finally gave up the idea.
findings.source: Chapter 940, Baek Yeon’s account of the Great Faction War

findings.current: There wasn’t a single martial artist to be found in Zhejiang Province, where the imperial capital stood—not even a sect.
findings.defect: The absolute claim contradicts the martial artists already traveling with Taekyung in Zhejiang.
findings.rationale: Keeps the point that Zhejiang offers no sect-based reinforcements without denying the presence of the party’s martial artists.
findings.replacement: There wasn’t a single Murim sect to call on in Zhejiang Province, where the imperial capital stood.
findings.source: Chapter 943, Taekyung’s assessment of potential reinforcements

summary: The packet’s voice, terminology, hooks, and active state are largely consistent. Two English passages warrant correction for clarity and internal consistency.
